questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : Methyl orange is a weak acid.
Statement-II : The benzenoid form of methyl orange is more intense/deeply coloured than the quinonoid form.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Methyl orange is a weak acid. Additionally, in acidic conditions, methyl orange exists in the quinonoid form, which is red in color. In alkaline conditions, it exists in the benzenoid form, which is yellow in color.& Since red is more deeply coloured than yellow, Statement-2 is wrong.

questions.q: The ${K}_{sp}$ for bismuth sulphide  \left({Bi}_{2}{S}_{3}\right)$ is $1 . 08 \times {10}^{- 73}$. The solubility of ${Bi}_{2}{S}_{3}$ in ${molL}^{- 1}$ at~$298K$& is$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${Bi}_{2}{S}_{3}$~will get dissociated as:

${Bi}_{2}{S}_{3} ⇌ 2{Bi}^{+ 3} + 3S^{- 2}2s3s$

Here,

~${K}_{sp} = \left(2s\right)2\left(3s\right)3 = 108s^{5}s = \left(\dfrac{Ksp}{108}\right)\dfrac{1}{5}s = \left(\dfrac{1 . 08 \times {10}^{- 73}}{108}\right)\dfrac{1}{5}s = {10}^{- 15}molL^{- 1}$

questions.q: Which of the following is strongest Bronsted base?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Bronsted base are those which can donate its lone pair to $H^{+}$ ion. The more easily the compound can donate its lone pair to $H^{+}$ strong will be a basic character.

Option D, is the strongest Bronsted base due to the availability of a lone pair which does not involve in any resonance.

questions.q: A weak acid HA has degree of dissociation x . Which option gives the correct expression of ( pH $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ )?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\left[\mathrmH^{+}\right](\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{C}(1-\mathrm{x})} \\ & {\left[\mathrmH^{+}\right]=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}} \frac{(1-\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{x}}} \\ & \log \mathrmH^{+}=\log \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}+\log \left(\frac{1-\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}}\right) \\ & -\log \mathrmH^{+}=-\log \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}-\log \frac{1-\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}} \\ & \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}-\log \frac{1-\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}} \\ & \mathrm{pH}-\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}=\log \frac{\mathrm{x}}{1-\mathrm{x}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Class $XII$ students were asked to prepare one litre of buffer solution of $pH8 . 26$ by their chemistry teacher. The amount of ammonium chloride to be dissolved by the student in $0 . 2M$ ammonia solution to make one litre of the buffer is (Given ${pK}_{b}\left({NH}_{3}\right) = 4 . 74;$ Molar mass of ${NH}_{3} = 17g{mol}^{- 1}$.~Molar mass of ${NH}_{4}Cl = 53 . 5g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
A mixture of ${NH}_{3}$~and ${NH}_{4}Cl$ will form a basic buffer.

$pH$~of final solution $= 8 . 26$

$pOH$~of final solution$= 14 - 8 . 26= 5 . 74$

Let the number of moles of ${NH}_{4}Cl$ added to $1L$ solution of be $x$.

Using Henderson’s equation.

$pOH = {pK}_{b} + \log \left[{NH}_{4}Cl\right]\left[{NH}_{3}\right]

$5 . 74 = 4 . 74 + $log\dfrac{x}{0 . 2}

$∴ x = 2$

The amount of ammonium chloride to be dissolved by the student in~$0 . 2M$~ammonia solution to make one litre of buffer$=2 $\times$53 . 5 = 107g$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Aqueous solution of ammonium carbonate is basic.
Statement (II) : Acidic/basic nature of salt solution of a salt of weak acid and weak base depends on ${K}_{a}$ and ${K}_{b}$ value of acid and the base forming it.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Aqueous solution of $( {NH}_{4}{)}_{2}{CO}_{3}$ is Basic.

$pH$ of salt of weak acid and weak base depends on ${K}_{a}$ and ${K}_{b}$ value of acid and the base forming it.

Solution is basic if

${K}_{b}$(weak base) >${K}_{a}$(weak acid).

${K}_{a}$(${HCO}_{3}^{-}$)=$4 . 3 \times {10}^{- 13}$

${K}_{b} ( {NH}_{4}OH )=1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}$

${K}_{b}$ (Ammonium hydroxide) >${Ka}_{}$(Hydrogen carbonate)

∴ Hence, solution of Ammonium carbonate is basic in nature.

Hence Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.q: $A student needs to prepare a buffer solution of propanoic acid and its sodium salt with $pH4$. The ratio of  \left[{CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}{COO}^{-}\right] \left[{CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}COOH\right]$ required to make buffer is Given :~${K}_{a}\left({CH}_{3}{CH}_{2}COOH\right) = 1 . 3 \times {10}^{- 5}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
& Henderson's equation for calculating& pH of acidic buffer solutions is given as

$pH = {pK}_{a} + \log \left( \left[$Salt\right]\left[Acid\right]\right)$

$pH = {pK}_{a} + \log \left( \left[{CH}_{3}{COO}^{-}\right]\left[{CH}_{3}$COOH\right]\right)$

$4 = 5 - \log ( 1 . 3 ) + \log \left( \left[{CH}_{3}{COO}^{-}\right]\left[{CH}_{3}COOH\right]\right)$

$\log \left($1 . 3 $\times {10}^{- 1}\right) =$=\log \left( \left[{CH}_{3}{COO}^{-}\right] \left[{CH}_{3}COOH\right]\right)$

\left[{CH}_{3}{COO}^{-}\right]\left[{CH}_{3}COOH\right] = 0 . 13$

questions.subject: Chemistry

${\text{k}}_{a} = \dfrac{C{\alpha}^{2}}{\left(1 - \alpha\right)}$

questions.q: Solubility of calcium phosphate (molecular mass, $M$) in water is ${W}_{g}$ per $100mL$ at $25 ° C .$ Its solubility product at $25 ° C$ will be approximately.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given the solubility of ${Ca}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2$ is $Wg / 100mL$. The solubility in $mol / L$ is $S = \dfrac{W}{M} \times \dfrac{1000}{100}mol / L$.

The equilibrium reaction of calcium phosphate is

$\begin{cases} & {Ca}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2 & \overset{}{⇌} & 3{Ca}^{2 +} & + & 2{PO}_{4}^{3 -} \\ Atequilibrium & & & 3S & & 2S\end{cases}$

Now, ${K}_{sp} = \left[{Ca}^{2 +}\right]3\left[{PO}_{4}^{3 -}\right]2$

$⇒ {K}_{sp} = \left(3S\right)3\left(2S\right)2 = 108 \times S^{5}$

$⇒ {K}_{sp} = 108 \times \left(\dfrac{W}{M} \times 10\right)5 ⇒ {K}_{sp} = 108 \times {10}^{5} \times \left(\dfrac{W}{M}\right)5$

$= 1 . 08 \times {10}^{7}\left(\dfrac{W}{M}\right)5$

questions.q: When the hydrogen ion concentration  \left[H^{+}\right]$changes by a factor of $1000$ , the value of $pH$ of the solution$

questions.solution:

$∴ \left[H^{+}\right]i = 1 ⇒ pH = 0$

It changes by 1000 units

$∴ \left[H^{+}\right]f = {10}^{3} ⇒ pH = - 3$

So, pH decreases by 3 units.

questions.q: If the solubility product of $PbS$ is $8 \times {10}^{- 28}$, then the solubility of $PbS$ in pure water at $298K$ is $x \times {10}^{- 16}molL^{- 1}$. The value of $x$~is____ (Nearest integer) [Given~$\sqrt{2} = 1 . 41$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$PbS \left(s\right)\overset{}{⇌}{Pb}^{2 +}\left(aq\right) + S^{2 -}\left(aq\right)$

Let us consider the solubility of $PbS$~is "$S$" $M$.

Thus,

Solubility product $= \left[{Pb}^{2 +} \left($aq\right)\right]\left[S^{2 -} \left(aq\right)\right]$

$Ksp = \left[{Pb}^{2 +} \left($aq\right)\right]\left[$S^{2 -}\left($aq\right)\right] ⋯ \left($i\right)$

We know

${K}_{sp} = S^{2}$

$S = $\sqrt{{K}_{sp}} = \sqrt{8 \times {10}^{- 28}} =$2$\sqrt{2} \times {10}^{- 14}

$= 2 . 82 $\times {10}^{- 14}

$= 282 \times {10}^{- 16}$

$

questions.q:
$20mL$ of $0 . 1MNaOH$ is added to $50mL$ of $0 . 1M$ acetic acid solution. The $pH$ of the resulting solution is $\times {10}^{- 2}$. (Nearest integer) Given : $pKa\left({CH}_{3}COOH\right) = 4 . 76$

$\log 2 = 0 . 30$

$\log 3 = 0 . 48$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When a strong base is added to a weak acid solution, it results in the formation of a salt. Here, acid is present in a limiting reagent and base is present in excess amounts. So, by using the pH formula:

$\begin{cases}pH & = & pKa + \log \left[salt\right]\left[acid\right]\end{cases}$

${CH}_{3}COOH + NaOH ⟶ {CH}_{3}COONa + {H}_{2}O52 — — 302$

$pH = {pK}_{a} + \log \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)

$pH = 4 . 76 + 0 . 30 - 0 . 48$

$= 4 . 76 – . 18$

$= 4 . 58$

$
